Large Language Model.explanation: LLMs are AI trained on massive text data to understand and generate human language
points: Built on transformer architecture with billions to trillions of parameters
Pre-trained on internet-scale corpora then fine-tuned for specific tasks
Capabilities include text generation, translation, summarization, question answering
Frontier models like GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5 set new benchmarks
Deployment challenges: high inference cost, hallucinations, ethical concerns

Transformer.explanation: The Transformer architecture revolutionized AI with powerful self-attention mechanisms
points: Introduced in 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need'
Encoder-decoder structure with multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers
Positional encodings enable parallel processing of sequences
Foundation for virtually all modern LLMs and vision models (ViT)

Tokens.explanation: Tokens are the smallest text units LLMs process — roughly 0.75 words per token
points: Subword tokenization (BPE, WordPiece) handles rare words and morphology
Token count determines context length and cost (pay per token)
Efficient tokenization critical for performance — Hugging Face tokenizers standard

Context Window.explanation: The context window is how much text an LLM can read and remember in one conversation
points: Measured in tokens — frontier models up to 1M+ (Gemini 1.5 Pro)
Limits total input + output length per request
Longer contexts enable better reasoning over documents/books/codebases
Techniques like RoPE, ALiBi extend effective context
Memory usage quadratic in context length — major inference bottleneck

Prompt Engineering.explanation: Prompt engineering is crafting inputs to reliably get the best outputs from LLMs
points: Techniques: few-shot examples, chain-of-thought, role-playing, delimiters
System prompt sets behavior; user prompt provides task
Iterative refinement with A/B testing prompts
Tools like LangChain, DSPy automate complex prompting
Critical skill as models improve but still sensitive to input phrasing

Fine-tuning.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained LLM to a specific domain, task, or writing style
points: Full fine-tuning updates all parameters — compute-intensive
PEFT methods (LoRA, adapters) update small fraction efficiently
Catastrophic forgetting mitigated by merging or continued pre-training
Cloud platforms (HF Spaces, Vertex AI) simplify fine-tuning workflows

Embeddings.explanation: Embeddings are numerical vectors that capture the meaning of text for AI search and retrieval
points: Dense vectors (768–4096 dims) from LLM encoder layers
Used for RAG, clustering, recommendation, classification
Multilingual and multimodal embeddings expanding use cases

Hallucination.explanation: LLM hallucination is when the model generates confident but factually incorrect answers
points: Caused by training data gaps, overgeneralization, or stochastic sampling
Mitigation: grounding with RAG, confidence scores, fact-checking chains
Benchmarks: TruthfulQA, HaluEval measure hallucination rates
Worse on rare facts or when pressured to answer uncertainly
Ongoing research in self-correction and uncertainty estimation

Temperature.explanation: Temperature controls how creative or random an LLM's output is — higher means more creative
points: Scales logits before softmax — temp 0 = deterministic, temp 1 = default
Lower temp for factual tasks (0.2–0.7), higher for creative (0.8–1.5)
Combined with top-p/top-k for better control
Affects diversity in generation but not base capability
API parameter in most inference engines

System Prompt.explanation: A system prompt sets the AI assistant's role, persona, rules, and constraints upfront
points: Invisible to user but guides all responses
Enforces behavior: 'You are a helpful assistant', safety rules
Can include response format instructions (JSON, bullet points)
Length counts toward context — keep concise
Advanced: dynamic system prompts for agents

Pre-training.explanation: Pre-training is the initial phase where a model learns language patterns from massive text corpora
points: Masked language modeling (BERT) or next-token prediction (GPT)
Datasets: CommonCrawl, Books, Wikipedia, code (The Pile)
Compute-intensive: frontier models use 10,000+ GPUs for months
Continued pre-training adapts to new domains

RLHF.explanation: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback aligns LLMs to human preferences and values
points: Three steps: SFT, reward model, PPO optimization
Human raters compare outputs for helpfulness/harmlessness
Alternatives: DPO, KTO eliminate RL step
Scalability challenge — expensive human data collection

RLAIF.explanation: RLAIF uses AI feedback instead of human feedback to align language models at scale
points: Uses stronger AI to label preferences
Reduces cost and bias from human raters
Shown comparable to RLHF in many cases

Constitutional AI.explanation: Constitutional AI trains models using a set of principles to guide safe and helpful behavior
points: AI critiques and revises responses based on principles
Reduces harmful outputs without human feedback

Instruction Tuning.explanation: Instruction tuning trains LLMs to follow natural language instructions reliably
points: Creates generalist models from base LLMs

Chain-of-Thought.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting makes LLMs reason step by step for more accurate answers
points: 'Let's think step by step' magic phrase

Few-shot Prompting.explanation: Few-shot prompting gives the LLM several examples in the prompt to guide its responses
points: 1–5 examples typically sufficient for large models

Zero-shot Prompting.explanation: Zero-shot prompting asks the LLM to complete a task with no examples given
points: Works well for simple classification, translation
Weaker than few-shot for novel tasks

Top-p Sampling.explanation: Top-p (nucleus) sampling limits word choices to the smallest set covering p probability mass
points: Dynamic k — adapts to distribution sharpness
Preferred over top-k in many setups

Top-k Sampling.explanation: Top-k sampling restricts the model to only choose from the k most likely next tokens
points: Can produce repetition in flat distributions
Early decoding method; top-p often better

Beam Search.explanation: Beam search keeps multiple candidate sequences and picks the most probable final output
points: Beam width (num_beams) trades quality vs compute
Length penalty and n-gram blocking avoid repetition
Higher quality but less diverse than sampling
Used in production for deterministic outputs

Greedy Decoding.explanation: Greedy decoding always picks the single most likely next token at every step
points: Can get stuck in suboptimal sequences
Often produces repetitive or generic text
Equivalent to beam search with beam=1

Tokenizer.explanation: A tokenizer converts text into numerical tokens that the model can process
points: Mismatch between train/inference tokenizers causes issues

BPE.explanation: Byte Pair Encoding builds a vocabulary by iteratively merging the most frequent character pairs

SentencePiece.explanation: SentencePiece is a language-independent tokenization library used by many modern LLMs
points: Treats space as character — no word splitting
Used in T5, ALBERT, XLNet, Llama

Padding.explanation: Padding adds dummy tokens to make all sequences the same length in a batch
points: Reduces waste vs fixed max length

Truncation.explanation: Truncation cuts sequences that exceed the maximum context length of the model
points: Truncate from left, right, or longest_first
Summarization or chunking for long texts

Logits.explanation: Logits are raw unnormalized scores the model assigns to each possible next token
points: Output of final linear layer (hidden_size → vocab_size)
Higher logit = higher probability after softmax
Logit bias API adds/subtracts from specific tokens

Softmax.explanation: Softmax converts logits into a probability distribution over the vocabulary

Cross-attention.explanation: Cross-attention lets the decoder attend to encoder representations in sequence-to-sequence tasks
points: Keys/values from encoder, queries from decoder
Replaced by prefix-LM in decoder-only models

Causal Masking.explanation: Causal masking prevents the model from attending to future tokens during training

Inference.explanation: Inference is the process of running a trained LLM to generate predictions or responses
points: Autoregressive generation: predict one token at a time
Batching for throughput vs single for latency
Frameworks: Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM
Cost dominated by GPU memory and compute

Quantization LLM.explanation: Quantization reduces LLM weight precision to run large models on smaller hardware
points: 2–4x memory reduction with minimal accuracy loss

Tensor Parallelism.explanation: Tensor parallelism splits model tensors across multiple GPUs to fit very large models
points: Combined with pipeline and data parallelism

Pipeline Parallelism.explanation: Pipeline parallelism splits model layers across GPUs so each GPU handles different layers
points: Bubble time inefficiency mitigated by interleaving
Used in training very deep models

Model Serving.explanation: Model serving hosts LLMs in production to handle real-time inference requests at scale
points: Frameworks: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server

vLLM.explanation: vLLM is an efficient LLM inference engine using PagedAttention for high throughput serving
points: PagedAttention shares KV cache across requests
Supports tensor parallel and pipeline parallel
Open-source from UC Berkeley LMSYS Org

Ollama.explanation: Ollama lets you run open-source LLMs locally on your laptop with a simple command
points: Supports Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Phi, etc.

LLaMA.explanation: Meta's LLaMA is an open-weight large language model series used by researchers worldwide
points: LlamaIndex and LangChain built around it
Commercial license restrictions lifted in Llama 3

GPT.explanation: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) is OpenAI's family of influential language models
points: GPT-1 (2018), GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o
Few-shot and zero-shot capabilities emerged at scale
Closed-source but API access widely available

Claude.explanation: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant family trained to be helpful, harmless, and honest
points: Strong in coding and long-form reasoning

Gemini.explanation: Gemini is Google DeepMind's multimodal AI model family competing with GPT and Claude

Mistral.explanation: Mistral is a French AI startup making efficient high-quality open-weight language models

Phi.explanation: Microsoft's Phi models are surprisingly capable small language models trained on high-quality data
points: Strong coding and reasoning for size

Qwen.explanation: Qwen is Alibaba's family of open-weight multilingual large language models

DeepSeek.explanation: DeepSeek is a Chinese LLM series that achieved GPT-4-level performance at far lower cost

Reward Model.explanation: A reward model scores LLM outputs for quality, helpfulness, and safety during RLHF training
points: Used in PPO to guide policy updates
Multiple reward heads for different objectives
Critical for alignment but can encode biases

Constitutional Principles.explanation: Constitutional principles are explicit rules an AI uses to critique and improve its own outputs
points: Reduces need for human feedback data

Red-teaming.explanation: Red-teaming adversarially tests LLMs to find safety failures before deployment

Model Card.explanation: A model card documents what an AI model can do, how it was trained, and known limitations
points: Sections: intended use, factors, evaluation data

System 2 Thinking.explanation: System 2 AI mimics slow deliberate reasoning rather than fast instinctive responses
points: Inspired by Kahneman's Thinking Fast and Slow

Reasoning Model.explanation: Reasoning models think step by step internally before producing a final answer
points: Spends more compute on hard problems
Strong on math, coding, science benchmarks

Mixture of Experts Routing.explanation: MoE routing gates select which expert sub-networks handle each input token dynamically
points: Learned router with load balancing loss

Sliding Context.explanation: Sliding context moves a fixed-size window across very long documents for extended processing
points: Used in long-document QA and summarization
Can lose global context without summaries

Long Context LLM.explanation: Long context models like Gemini 1.5 can process over a million tokens in one pass
points: Sparse attention and KV cache optimizations
Applications: code repos, long videos, legal docs
Still quadratic cost — selective attention emerging

Prompt Caching.explanation: Prompt caching stores computed activations for repeated prompt prefixes to save cost and latency
points: Saves KV cache for system prompt/shared context
Dramatic speed-up for multi-turn and agents

Structured Output LLM.explanation: Structured output forces LLMs to respond in valid JSON or a specified schema every time

Function Calling.explanation: Function calling lets LLMs invoke structured external functions based on natural language requests
points: Model outputs JSON with function name + args
Execute function and feed result back

Tool Use.explanation: Tool use enables LLMs to call external APIs, search the web, and run code during reasoning
points: Multi-step: decide tool, call, observe, reason

Multi-turn Conversation.explanation: Multi-turn conversations maintain context across many message exchanges in a session

Safety Training.explanation: Safety training teaches LLMs to refuse harmful requests and add caveats to dangerous content
